event.title: UnitedHealth Group executive or employee sentenced to imprisonment in a DOJ case
event.proposition: A federal court sentences a UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare executive or employee to imprisonment on criminal charges brought by the Department of Justice in connection with its antitrust investigation of UnitedHealth Group or the Change Healthcare cyberattack.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a federal court judgment that imposes a sentence of imprisonment on a UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare executive or employee, on criminal charges brought by the Department of Justice arising from the DOJ antitrust investigation of UnitedHealth Group or from the Change Healthcare cyberattack. A civil antitrust suit, a consent decree, a corporate fine or corporate plea, an indictment or conviction without a custodial sentence, and any sentence of a person outside these companies (for example a ransomware actor) do not count.

event.asset: Change Healthcare cyberattack and protected health information breach (February 2024)
event.title: HIPAA penalties over the Change Healthcare breach exceed $40 million
event.proposition: HIPAA civil money penalties or settlement payments imposed by HHS Office for Civil Rights on UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare over the Change Healthcare breach total more than $40 million.
event.criterion: Resolved on the HHS Office for Civil Rights enforcement listing (resolution agreements and civil money penalties) only. TRUE on the date the cumulative monetary amount of HHS OCR civil money penalties and resolution-agreement settlement payments that name UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare and concern the Change Healthcare breach first exceeds $40,000,000. Direction: above; threshold in the forecaster's words: 'a $40 million ransom payment would be trivial next to'. State attorney general actions, private settlements, FTC or SEC penalties and the ransom itself do not count. If HHS OCR has published no such action 12 months after the deadline, the event is unresolvable.

resolution_source.name: HHS Office for Civil Rights enforcement actions (resolution agreements and civil money penalties)

quantity.metric: cumulative HHS OCR HIPAA civil money penalties and settlement payments imposed on UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare over the Change Healthcare breach
quantity.series: HHS Office for Civil Rights enforcement actions listing (resolution agreements and civil money penalties)

readings: 'the fines on the HIPAA breach' = HIPAA monetary penalties imposed by the HIPAA enforcer, HHS Office for Civil Rights; settlement payments under an OCR resolution agreement count as fines. State attorney general HIPAA actions are excluded to keep one resolution source.

'financially catastrophic in a way that a $40 million ransom payment would be trivial next to' is read at its lowest threshold: more than $40 million. The reading favours the forecaster; the words imply a much larger amount.

condition.asset: Change Healthcare cyberattack (February 2024): timing of UnitedHealth Group's knowledge of the intrusion
condition.entity: HHS Office for Civil Rights; federal court; US Congress
condition.title: Documentation shows UnitedHealth Group knew of the Change Healthcare intrusion before it disclosed it
condition.proposition: A public regulator finding, court filing, congressional record or company filing documents that UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare knew of the Change Healthcare intrusion before its first public disclosure of the incident.
condition.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public document that states, with reference to records, that UnitedHealth Group, Optum or Change Healthcare knew of the intrusion before its first public disclosure of the incident: an HHS Office for Civil Rights resolution agreement, notice of proposed determination or civil money penalty notice; a filed court order or finding; sworn congressional testimony or a committee report; or a UnitedHealth Group SEC filing. Speculation in press reports, unverified claims by the attackers and allegations in complaints not yet adjudicated do not count.

resolution_source.name: HHS Office for Civil Rights enforcement actions; federal court dockets (CourtListener); congressional committee records; SEC EDGAR

readings: 'documentation that they knew before' = documented knowledge of the intrusion earlier than the company's first public disclosure, per the immediate context ('knew of the intrusion earlier than reported').
'they' = UnitedHealth Group and its subsidiaries Optum and Change Healthcare.
